questions.question: How do Spring Data JPA repositories work, and how do you use derived queries, @Query, and Specifications effectively?
questions.title: Spring Data JPA — Repositories, Derived Queries, @Query, Specifications
questions.direct_answer: **Spring Data JPA generates repository implementations at startup** by scanning interfaces extending `Repository<T, ID>` (typically `JpaRepository<T, ID>`) and creating proxy implementations backed by **`SimpleJpaRepository`**. You get CRUD, `Pageable`, and `Sort` for free. Custom methods come from three places: **(1) derived queries** (`findByStatusAndCreatedAtAfter(...)` parsed from method name); **(2) `@Query("JPQL" or "native")`** for explicit queries; **(3) `Specification<T>`** (with `JpaSpecificationExecutor`) for dynamic predicates. Use **DTO/interface projections** to avoid loading full entities, **`@EntityGraph`** to kill N+1, and **`@Modifying`** for bulk UPDATE/DELETE. Gotchas: derived queries explode beyond 3-4 parameters, `Page<T>` runs an extra `COUNT` (use `Slice<T>` for large datasets), and native queries skip JPQL features and lose pagination unless you supply `countQuery`.

interviewer_intent.testing: Real Spring Data JPA usage; custom queries; dynamic queries; projections
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Derived query method-name explosion; fetching full entity when only columns needed; forgetting `@Modifying` on UPDATE/DELETE
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Discuss `Specification`, Query By Example, interface vs class projections, `Page` vs `Slice` performance, and Hibernate 6 enhancements

sections.title: How Spring Data JPA Magic Works
sections.content:
**You declare an interface:**

```java
public interface OrderRepository extends JpaRepository<Order, Long> { }
```

**At startup**, Spring scans for these interfaces and generates proxy implementations backed by `SimpleJpaRepository`. You get for free: `save`, `saveAll`, `findById`, `findAll`, `count`, `delete`, `deleteById`, `Page<T> findAll(Pageable)`, plus `Sort` support.

**Three custom-query mechanisms:**
- **Derived queries** parsed from the method name (`findByStatus`, `countByCustomerId`).
- **`@Query`** annotation for explicit JPQL or native SQL.
- **`Specification<T>`** (with `JpaSpecificationExecutor`) for dynamic queries built programmatically.

**Other features worth knowing:**
- **Query By Example (QBE)** — match by example prototype.
- **Interface-based projections** — lightweight DTOs without `SELECT NEW`.
- **Entity graphs** — declarative fetch plans (`@EntityGraph`).
- **Auditing** — `@CreatedDate`, `@LastModifiedBy` via `@EnableJpaAuditing`.
- **`@Modifying`** for UPDATE/DELETE queries.

sections.title: Derived Queries — Power and Limits
sections.content:
**Method-name syntax rules:**
- Start with `findBy`, `readBy`, `queryBy`, `getBy`, `countBy`, `existsBy`, `deleteBy`.
- Combine with `And`, `Or`.
- Operators: `Between`, `LessThan`, `GreaterThan`, `GreaterThanEqual`, `IsNull`, `Like`, `StartingWith`, `Containing`, `In`, `NotIn`, `True`, `False`, `IgnoreCase`.
- Modifiers: `OrderByXxxAsc/Desc`, `Distinct`, `First`, `Top<N>`.

**Example collection:**

```java
List<Order> findByStatus(OrderStatus status);
List<Order> findByStatusIn(Collection<OrderStatus> statuses);
List<Order> findByCustomerIdAndStatusAndAmountGreaterThan(
    Long cid, OrderStatus s, BigDecimal minAmount);
List<Order> findTop10ByCustomerIdOrderByCreatedAtDesc(Long cid);
Optional<Order> findFirstByOrderByCreatedAtDesc();
Page<Order> findByStatus(OrderStatus s, Pageable p);
Slice<Order> findByStatusOrderByCreatedAtDesc(OrderStatus s, Pageable p);
Stream<Order> findByStatusOrderByCreatedAt(OrderStatus s);
```

**When to stop using derived queries:**
- Method name exceeds 3-4 parameters.
- Optional filters (some null, some not).
- Joins across multiple entities.
- Aggregations / calculations.
- Complex OR logic.

**Page vs Slice vs List performance:**
- **`Page<T>`** runs the data query + extra `count(*)` — expensive on huge tables.
- **`Slice<T>`** fetches one extra row to decide `hasNext()` — cheaper.
- **`List<T>`** for full unpaged results — only for small result sets.
- **Cursor-based pagination** (`WHERE id > :lastId ORDER BY id LIMIT N`) for huge tables.

sections.title: @Query, Projections, and @Modifying
Specifications and Entity Graphs for Dynamic and Eager Loading
Auditing, Transactions, Pitfalls, and Best Practices
Key Points
sections.content:
- **`extends JpaRepository<T, ID>`** = CRUD + `Pageable` + `Sort` for free.
- **Derived queries** for short, static method names; switch to `@Query` or `Specification` past 3-4 parameters.
- **`@Query(JPQL)`** preferred; `nativeQuery = true` for DB-specific SQL.
- **`Specification<T>`** + `JpaSpecificationExecutor` for dynamic optional filters.
- **Projections** — `SELECT new ...` constructor expressions or interface-based.
- **`@Modifying`** required on UPDATE/DELETE `@Query`.
- **`Page` runs COUNT** — use `Slice` or cursor pagination for large tables.
- **`@EntityGraph` + `JOIN FETCH`** kill N+1.
- **Auditing** via `AuditingEntityListener` + `@EnableJpaAuditing`.
- **Read services** — `@Transactional(readOnly = true)`.

sections.title: How to Answer This Verbally
sections.content:
Spring Data JPA generates implementations of your repository interfaces at startup. You extend `JpaRepository<T, ID>` and get CRUD for free; custom methods come from three mechanisms.

**The three mechanisms:**
- **Derived queries** parsed from the method name (`findByStatusAndCreatedAtAfter`)
- **`@Query`** annotation with JPQL or native SQL
- **`Specification<T>`** with `JpaSpecificationExecutor` for dynamic predicates

**When to stop using derived queries:**
- Method name > 3-4 parameters
- Optional filters
- Aggregations
- Complex OR logic

**Page vs Slice:**
- `Page<T>` runs `count(*)` for total pages — slow on huge tables
- `Slice<T>` skips the count — uses 'fetch one extra to know hasNext'
- For very large tables: cursor-based pagination

**Projections** avoid loading full entities — interface (closed: only declared columns; open: full entity + SpEL) or class-based with `SELECT new`.

**`@Modifying`** required on UPDATE/DELETE `@Query`; `clearAutomatically=true` and `flushAutomatically=true` keep the persistence context consistent.

**N+1**: prevent with `@EntityGraph`, `JOIN FETCH`, or DTO projections.

**Auditing**: `@EnableJpaAuditing`, `@EntityListeners(AuditingEntityListener.class)` on a `@MappedSuperclass` with `@CreatedDate`, `@LastModifiedDate`, `@CreatedBy`, `@LastModifiedBy`.

questions.title: JpaRepository vs CrudRepository vs PagingAndSortingRepository
questions.question: What is the difference between `JpaRepository`, `CrudRepository`, and `PagingAndSortingRepository`, and which should you extend?
questions.direct_answer: Spring Data defines a hierarchy of repository interfaces — pick the one whose contract matches your need. **`Repository<T, ID>`** is the empty marker interface enabling Spring Data scanning. **`CrudRepository<T, ID>`** adds CRUD methods (`save`, `findById`, `findAll`, `delete`). **`PagingAndSortingRepository<T, ID>`** (since Spring Data 3 it is **separate** from `CrudRepository`) adds `findAll(Pageable)` and `findAll(Sort)`. **`JpaRepository<T, ID>`** combines CRUD + paging + JPA-specific methods (`flush()`, `saveAllAndFlush()`, `getReferenceById()`, `deleteAllInBatch()`). For most JPA apps, **extend `JpaRepository`**. Extend `CrudRepository` (with separate `PagingAndSortingRepository` if needed) when you want a smaller surface area, persistence-tech portability, or do not need JPA-specific methods.

sections.title: Repository Hierarchy — Pick the Smallest Surface That Meets the Need
sections.content:
Spring Data ships a layered hierarchy of repository interfaces. Each layer adds capability and exposes more methods. **Picking deliberately matters** because the interface you extend becomes part of your service contract — every method you inherit is publicly callable.

**The hierarchy (Spring Data 3+):**
- **`Repository<T, ID>`** — empty marker; activates Spring Data infrastructure.
- **`CrudRepository<T, ID>`** — `save`, `saveAll`, `findById`, `existsById`, `findAll`, `findAllById`, `count`, `deleteById`, `delete`, `deleteAllById`, `deleteAll`.
- **`ListCrudRepository<T, ID>`** (Spring Data 3) — same as `CrudRepository` but methods return `List<T>` instead of `Iterable<T>`.
- **`PagingAndSortingRepository<T, ID>`** — `findAll(Sort)`, `findAll(Pageable)`. **No longer extends `CrudRepository` in Spring Data 3.**
- **`JpaRepository<T, ID>`** — combines `ListCrudRepository` + `ListPagingAndSortingRepository` + JPA-specific methods (`flush`, `saveAndFlush`, `saveAllAndFlush`, `getReferenceById`, `deleteAllInBatch`, `deleteInBatch`).

**For most JPA apps**, extending `JpaRepository` is the pragmatic default.

sections.title: Methods and Capabilities — What Each Interface Adds
sections.content:
Quick reference for what each level provides.

| Interface | CRUD | Pagination/Sort | JPA-specific (flush, batch, getReference) | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Repository<T, ID>` | No | No | No | (marker only) |
| `CrudRepository<T, ID>` | Yes | No | No | `Iterable<T>` |
| `ListCrudRepository<T, ID>` | Yes | No | No | `List<T>` |
| `PagingAndSortingRepository<T, ID>` | No (Spring Data 3) | Yes | No | `Page<T>` / `Iterable<T>` |
| `ListPagingAndSortingRepository<T, ID>` | No | Yes | No | `Page<T>` / `List<T>` |
| `JpaRepository<T, ID>` | Yes | Yes | Yes | `List<T>` |

**Spring Data 3 breaking change:**
- In Spring Data 2.x, `PagingAndSortingRepository` extended `CrudRepository` — getting paging meant getting CRUD too.
- In Spring Data 3.x, **the inheritance was removed** so you can choose paging without CRUD or vice versa.
- Most apps still want both — extend `JpaRepository` (or compose `ListCrudRepository` + `ListPagingAndSortingRepository`).

sections.title: JPA-Specific Methods Worth Knowing on `JpaRepository`
sections.content:
**`flush()`:**
- Forces the persistence context to write pending changes to the database.
- Use before reading values that depend on triggers or sequences.

**`saveAndFlush(entity)`:**
- Saves and immediately flushes.
- Useful when subsequent code needs the database-side state in the same transaction.

**`saveAllAndFlush(entities)`:**
- Bulk save followed by flush.
- For batch use cases that need committed state visible immediately.

**`deleteAllInBatch()` / `deleteInBatch(entities)`:**
- Issues a single `DELETE` statement instead of N per-entity deletes.
- Bypasses cascading and lifecycle callbacks.
- For raw bulk cleanup; do not use when cascades or callbacks must fire.

**`getReferenceById(id)`:**
- Returns a Hibernate proxy without hitting the database.
- Useful for setting an FK without loading the parent entity.
  ```java
  Customer ref = customerRepo.getReferenceById(42L);
  Order o = new Order();
  o.setCustomer(ref);
  orderRepo.save(o);
  ```
- Throws `EntityNotFoundException` lazily on first attribute access.
- Avoids an unnecessary SELECT when you only need to satisfy a foreign key.

**`getOne(id)` (deprecated)** — same intent as `getReferenceById`; use the new name.

sections.title: When to Choose Each Interface
sections.content:
**When `JpaRepository` helps:**
- Standard JPA app; you want CRUD + paging + flush + batch in one place.
- Team is committed to JPA; portability is not a concern.
- Simplest path; fewest decisions.

**When `JpaRepository` hurts:**
- Library / framework code that should not impose JPA on consumers.
- Repository contract intentionally narrow (only `findById` + `save`).
- You want to swap to Spring Data Mongo / R2DBC / Cassandra later.

**When `CrudRepository` (or `ListCrudRepository`) helps:**
- Persistence-technology-neutral contracts.
- You explicitly do NOT want batch/flush leaking into the API.
- Microservice with one tiny aggregate root.

**When `CrudRepository` hurts:**
- You need pagination (Spring Data 3 — must add `PagingAndSortingRepository` separately).
- You need flush, batch, or `getReferenceById`.

**When `PagingAndSortingRepository` helps (alone):**
- Read-only repository with pagination/sort but no mutations.
- Reporting-style repositories.

**Watch for:**
- Every method inherited is part of your repository's public API. Consumers can call `deleteAll()` on a `JpaRepository` — sometimes a foot-gun.
- Restrict surface area with the `@RepositoryRestResource(exported = false)` (Spring Data REST) or by extending only `Repository<T, ID>` and re-declaring the methods you actually want.
- `getReferenceById` returns a proxy — accessing fields outside a transaction throws `LazyInitializationException`.
- `deleteAllInBatch()` skips cascade and `@PreRemove` — dangerous on entities with related data.

sections.title: Choosing the Right Interface in Practice
Key Points
sections.content:
- **`Repository<T, ID>`** is the empty marker; pick a smaller surface by extending it directly and re-declaring methods.
- **`CrudRepository`** adds basic CRUD with `Iterable<T>`; **`ListCrudRepository`** returns `List<T>`.
- **`PagingAndSortingRepository`** in Spring Data 3 no longer extends `CrudRepository` — choose explicitly.
- **`JpaRepository`** = CRUD + paging + JPA-specific (`flush`, batch, `getReferenceById`).
- **`getReferenceById`** returns a proxy — useful for FK assignment without an extra SELECT.
- **`deleteAllInBatch`** issues a single DELETE — skips cascade and callbacks.
- **Choose deliberately** — every inherited method becomes part of your public API.

sections.title: How to Answer This Verbally
sections.content:
Spring Data ships a hierarchy of repository interfaces.

**The hierarchy:**
- `Repository<T, ID>` — empty marker; activates Spring Data
- `CrudRepository<T, ID>` — basic CRUD
- `ListCrudRepository<T, ID>` — same but returns `List` instead of `Iterable`
- `PagingAndSortingRepository<T, ID>` — paging and sorting; in Spring Data 3 it is separate from CrudRepository
- `JpaRepository<T, ID>` — combines CRUD + paging + JPA-specific (`flush`, `saveAndFlush`, `getReferenceById`, `deleteAllInBatch`)

**Which to extend:**
- Standard JPA app -> `JpaRepository`
- Library code or persistence-tech neutral -> `CrudRepository` / `ListCrudRepository`
- Read-only repository with paging -> `PagingAndSortingRepository`
- Maximum control over the API surface -> extend `Repository<T, ID>` directly and re-declare the methods you want

**JPA-specific methods worth mentioning:**
- `getReferenceById` — returns a Hibernate proxy; useful for setting a FK without loading the parent
- `saveAndFlush` — forces immediate flush; useful when subsequent code needs DB-side state
- `deleteAllInBatch` — single DELETE; skips cascade and callbacks; raw bulk cleanup

**Spring Data 3 change:** `PagingAndSortingRepository` no longer extends `CrudRepository` — you can choose paging without CRUD, useful for read-only repositories.
